items.english: "You won't listen, will you." The young father gazed at the small round arms and at the child's eyes with long, dark lashes, moving nimbly, cleverly, without a pause, as if wondering what was to be done, and then with a smile over his whole face, pinching the child's round sticking-out cheek with his finger, he felt under the {t:table} for a big bowl as if searching and put it in her hand.
notes: Long p7-s2 kept as one additive sentence; face-full smile kept as smile for network. Her hand is the child's hand per referent map, rendered as her to keep ambiguity visible in context.

sentences: 若い父親は、その小さなまるい腕や、敏捷に怜悧にすきもなく動いてる、黒みがちの睫のながい子供の瞳をぢっと見てゐると、どうしたらいゝだらうといふやうに、やがて顔一ぱいな微笑を持って、子供のまるくつき出た頬を指で一寸つまみながら、大きな茶碗をテーブルの下から探すやうにしてとると、彼女の手に渡した。

alternatives.what_would_settle: Editor ruling on boya: keep Japanese Bōya versus plain-English address for Casual view.

items.english: She dished up the hot, freshly cooked {t:rice}, with white steam rising thick, from the pot and handed it to him. And her young big eyes too, full of a motherly gladness, gazed at the never for a moment still, lovely small-bird ways of the child. And as if she could not bear it, muttering to herself, 'Whatever is to be done with this child,' as if the child were dear beyond all managing, she said firmly, "{t:boya}," but a smile overflowed from her face, and she looked at the man's face as if asking for help. And the three, as if they had forgotten everything, smiled at each other over the child, as if wondering what to do for the child. And for the child, they set about the meal with a warm bustle, and with a smile and gladness welling up of itself on top of it. And with the clattering noise, they did not hear the sound of rain and wind.
notes: Boya left as {t:boya} token, not fixed to boy/girl. Smile kept throughout for s3 smile-overflow, s4 smile-at-each-other, s5 smile-and-gladness to hold network. Rain-wind sound kept literal and not tagged as {t:storm}; storm frame stays bare and linked.
Inner muttering rendered as single-quoted thought inside narration to keep outer "{t:boya}" address distinct.

sentences: 彼女は鍋から熱い炊き立ての、白い湯気が一ぱい立ち上ってる御飯をついで彼に渡した。
そして彼女の若い大きな瞳も、母親らしい嬉しさにみちて子供の瞬間もぢっとしてない、小鳥のやうに愛らしい様子を見つめた。
そして、たまらなささうに、この子はどうしたといふんだらう、とふと口の中に独言を云ひながら、どうにも仕方がない程可愛いといふやうな様子で、『坊や、』と強く云ったけれども、笑が顔からあふれて了って、彼女は助をかりるやうに男の顔を見た。
そして三人は、すべての事を忘れてしまった様に、子供の為めに互にどうしようかといふ様に笑ひ合った。
そして子供の為めに、彼等は暖かい賑かさと、其上に自然に溢れる笑ひと嬉しさを持って食事にとりかゝったのであった。
また彼等は、ごたごたした騒がしさの為に、雨風の音を耳にしない。

items.english: The young father spread his red, big hand busily over the {t:table}. And his eyes holding back the smile that welled up helplessly from the child, he held the child up and put a little food into that small red mouth. In the gaps, hastily opening his big mouth, he crammed {t:rice} into his own mouth.
notes: Red big hand and big mouth kept plain and physical against vision. Held-back smile kept as smile; crammed rice keeps warm staple versus cold potato contrast to come.

sentences: 若い父親は、彼の赤く大きな片手を忙しくテーブルの上に拡げてゐた。
そしてその眼は子供によって仕方がなく湧き出た笑を堪へながら、子供をさゝへて、その小さな赤い口に僅の食物を入れてやった。
そのすきに彼は、あわたゞしく大きな口を開けた、彼は彼自身の口のなかに御飯を押し込んだ。

data.say: Drafted p7-p9 in spare close voice, keeping table/rice/boya tokens, smile network, and literal noisy supper before the potato stillness.
